impact_pathways.impact_narrative: This project advances EI-01 through a jointly prepared Career Development Plan (D4-01, WP4/T4-01, due M3) that formalises structured transferable-skills training across MSCA-PF mandatory dimensions: digital and AI skills applied to probabilistic remote-sensing modelling and scientific coding, knowledge valorisation, research integrity, and FAIR open-science stewardship. The fellow's cross-disciplinary profile — coupling plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise with geoinformatics, hyperspectral and multi-sensor fusion methods acquired at ELTE (OUT-6, WP4/T4-02) — expands career options both within academia and in applied agri-tech sectors. The two-way knowledge transfer (plant physiology into ELTE's remote-sensing group; geoinformatics methods into the fellow's practice) produces a research profile that is distinctive at the intersection of disciplines and therefore more employable. Pathway is grounded in IMP-4 (MSCA-PF criterion 2.1 — career perspectives and employability), WP4, and deliverable D4-01.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: EI-02 is realised through two complementary project-specific mechanisms, both grounded in Tier 3 linkage data. First, IMP-1 (scientific advance in probabilistic multi-sensor crop-water-state estimation, METH-SOTA-007/006) exemplifies the interdisciplinary innovation culture: the probabilistic fusion diagnostic methodology (OUT-1, WP1/T1-02/T1-03) bridges Bayesian hierarchical modelling, radar/optical/PlanetScope remote sensing, and plant-physiology ground truth — disciplines that rarely co-occur in a single end-to-end pipeline. The Research Gap Matrix (METH-SOTA-007) identifies this cross-disciplinary gap as the specific empty cell the project targets. D1-01 (multi-sensor data harmonisation and diagnostic model report, WP1, due M14) is the primary deliverable of this interdisciplinary synthesis. Second, IMP-4 formalises the inter-institutional two-way knowledge transfer between the fellow and ELTE's geoinformatics and remote-sensing group (OUT-6, WP4/T4-01/T4-02, D4-01): the fellow's plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise enters ELTE's research culture, and the host's remote-sensing and hyperspectral fusion methods enter the fellow's practice. Together these produce a project-specific and traceable pathway to a strengthened interdisciplinary R&I culture.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: EI-03 is addressed via IMP-2 (economic and societal impact: water-use efficiency and farm resilience) and IMP-1's open dissemination strand. The uncertainty-aware AquaCrop decision engine (OUT-2, WP2/T2-01/T2-02) and the standalone research demonstrator web MVP (OUT-4, WP2/T2-03, TRL 3-4, RQ10) translate the project's probabilistic methodology into a tangible artefact that presents irrigation recommendations with honest uncertainty bounds to non-specialist users. Interaction with Hungarian tomato farmers through the associated partner AgroVIR (WP3 field validation sites) constitutes a direct and documented route to broadened public engagement with applied remote-sensing research. D2-01 (decision engine and research demonstrator report, WP2, due M20) is the primary output grounding this pathway. Dissemination to the geoinformatics community and farming sector is documented in D5-02 (dissemination and communication activity report, WP5/T5-02, due M24), traceable via IMP-1's WP5 linkage. Out-5 (open-access publications and FAIR data) broadens reach further through the scientific community. Pathway is grounded in IMP-2's linked_wp_ids [WP2, WP3] and IMP-1's linked WP5.

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: EI-05 is the broadest impact pathway, aggregating IMP-1 (scientific advance in probabilistic multi-sensor crop-water-state estimation) and IMP-4 (career and ERA advancement). IMP-1's outputs span the complete research pipeline — the probabilistic fusion diagnostic methodology (OUT-1, D1-01, WP1/T1-02/T1-03), the uncertainty-aware AquaCrop decision engine (OUT-2, D2-01, WP2/T2-01/T2-02), and the field validation uncertainty-calibration evidence (OUT-3, D3-01, WP3/T3-01/T3-03, targeting 90% prediction-interval coverage RQ5) — and are released under open-science principles via a FAIR data management plan (D5-01, WP5/T5-01, due M6) and dissemination report (D5-02, WP5/T5-02, due M24). Each released artefact — methods, calibrated models, open validation data (OUT-5) — increases the available stock of validated ERA resources for geoinformatics and precision-agriculture research communities. IMP-4 adds the knowledge-transfer dimension: the fellow's cross-disciplinary training at ELTE (OUT-6, D4-01, WP4) increases ELTE's R&I capacity and contributes a distinctively cross-disciplinary researcher to the ERA talent pool. All six Phase 3 deliverables are included because each is traceable to either IMP-1's linked_wp_ids [WP1,WP2,WP3,WP5] or IMP-4's linked_wp_ids [WP4].

impact_pathways.impact_narrative: EI-06 is addressed through IMP-4's two-way knowledge exchange at ELTE (WP4/T4-01/T4-02) and IMP-1's open dissemination strand (WP5). The fellow's plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise is introduced into ELTE's geoinformatics teaching and research environment, and ELTE's hyperspectral, multisensor-fusion and remote-sensing methods are embedded in the fellow's evolving practice. The Career Development Plan (D4-01, due M3) documents the structured training programme and supervision at ELTE, providing a formal mechanism through which evolving project results — probabilistic fusion diagnostics, AquaCrop uncertainty calibration, field validation evidence — are integrated into the host's academic context during the fellowship. dissemination_plan.open_access_policy: All peer-reviewed publications arising from the project will be made immediately open access upon acceptance, in compliance with MSCA open access mandates and Plan S where applicable; preprints will be deposited in discipline-relevant repositories (e.g., ESSOAr, arXiv). The calibrated Bayesian hierarchical fusion models, multi-sensor EO datasets, and AquaCrop uncertainty parameter posteriors produced in WP1, WP2, and WP3 will be archived under FAIR principles with persistent DOIs as specified in the project DMP (D5-01, WP5, due M6). Software artefacts, including the probabilistic fusion pipeline and the research demonstrator MVP, will be released under a permissive open-source licence (MIT or Apache 2.0). No embargo periods beyond those required by journal publishing agreements will be applied; the default is immediate open availability.

activities.expected_result: A reusable, documented probabilistic multi-sensor fusion-to-irrigation-decision framework available to the geoinformatics and precision-agriculture R&I community, enabling follow-on research targeting other crops and regions without repeating the fellowship's foundational derivation — directly increasing ERA R&I capacity (EI-05) by providing validated open artefacts that survive the fellowship duration
activities.timing: M20-M24: code and documentation released alongside open-access publication; persistent DOI infrastructure established via D5-01 data management plan by M24

activities.expected_result: The standalone uncertainty-aware irrigation-decision demonstrator (TRL 3-4, OUT-4, D2-01) serves as a documented proof-of-concept that the fellow and AgroVIR can reference in follow-on funding bids — e.g., EIC Pathfinder, national agricultural innovation funds, or Horizon Europe Cluster 6 calls — targeting operational TRL 5-6 deployment and broader water-use efficiency uptake (IMP-2)
activities.timing: M24: demonstrator documented in D2-01 by M20; exploitable as follow-on proposal reference from M24 onward; AgroVIR agronomic feedback documented as part of WP3 validation by M24

activities.expected_result: ELTE's geoinformatics and remote-sensing group gains durable embedded expertise in probabilistic crop-water-state modelling and non-destructive stress phenotyping through the structured two-way knowledge transfer (WP4/T4-02), expanding the host's capacity to supervise follow-on PhDs and postdoctoral researchers in agri-environmental EO and to compete for subsequent agri-EO grants leveraging the validated methodology
activities.timing: M1-M24: ongoing throughout fellowship; formalised in Career Development Plan D4-01 by M3 and recorded in training activity log updated at M12 and M24

exploitation_plan.ipr_strategy: The project produces academic research outputs at TRL 3-4; no patent applications are anticipated, and the primary exploitation route is open publication and open-source software release, consistent with MSCA open science requirements. AgroVIR agronomic validation datasets will be handled under data-sharing terms agreed between ELTE and AgroVIR and documented in the DMP (D5-01, WP5, due M6), ensuring the associated partner's proprietary agronomic data is protected while derived statistical parameters and calibration evidence remain publishable. Software artefacts and calibrated model outputs will be released under permissive open-source licences. Should the demonstrator yield a commercially exploitable feature during the fellowship, the fellow and ELTE will consult ELTE's technology transfer office to assess whether protection measures are warranted prior to public release.

sustainability_mechanism.description: Post-project sustainability of the project's results is secured through three complementary mechanisms grounded in project-specific deliverables and partner roles. First, all calibrated Bayesian multi-sensor fusion models, validated multi-sensor EO datasets, and AquaCrop uncertainty parameter posteriors are archived under FAIR principles with persistent DOIs via the DMP (D5-01, WP5, due M6), enabling the geoinformatics and precision-agriculture research community to build on the validated probabilistic fusion-to-decision methodology independently of the fellowship's continuation — directly sustaining IMP-1's scientific contribution beyond M24. Second, ELTE's geoinformatics and remote-sensing group retains the probabilistic multi-sensor fusion expertise and cross-disciplinary training infrastructure embedded through the two-way knowledge transfer in WP4 (OUT-6, D4-01, due M3), equipping the host to supervise follow-on research, co-author future proposals, and continue Route B landscape-compatible sensing methodology development beyond the 24-month project period — sustaining IMP-4's ERA capacity contribution. Third, the uncertainty-aware irrigation-decision demonstrator (TRL 3-4, OUT-4, D2-01, due M20) and its documented field validation evidence (D3-01, 90% prediction-interval coverage target RQ5; Route B covariation test RQ9) constitute a publicly available proof-of-concept that the fellow and AgroVIR can reference in follow-on funding bids targeting operational TRL 5-6 deployment, connecting IMP-2's water-use efficiency and IMP-3's landscape-compatible sensing co-benefit to longer-term uptake beyond the fellowship scope.
